ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended by the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act 1 of 2017 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (inserting ss 26A-26B on beneficial interest filing); Companies Regulations, 2011, as amended by the 2023 Beneficial Ownership Regulations; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act 12 of 2004. The CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register applies a 5% beneficial-interest reporting threshold, while the FIC accountable-institution due-diligence benchmark for beneficial ownership identification is 25% ownership or control.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners, and where contractually feasible key counterparties, against the FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions List implementing UN Security Council Resolutions 1267/1989 and 1373, the domestic South African PEP identification framework contained in FIC Guidance Note 7A, and the OFAC SDN and UK/EU consolidated sanctions lists given the USD and cross-border payment rails; enhanced due diligence is mandated for any foreign PEP, resident of a high-risk jurisdiction, or any sanctions nexus, with reasonable-step verification of source of wealth and the full beneficial ownership chain under FICA ss 21A-21H and POCDATARA s 28A.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services transactional portal (www.cipc.co.za; cservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; a foreign-language name must be accompanied by a transliteration or English translation and must not be identical or merely confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trademark; only one name is registered, with the optional suffix expression (Pty) Ltd being an acceptable and commonly used designation for a private company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: before expiry, the applicant may lodge a CIPC application for extension of the reserved name, which may be granted once for a further 60 days upon payment of the prescribed fee. Rejection: upon a formal notice of refusal, the applicant may request written reasons from CIPC and, within 20 business days of the refusal notice, lodge an application with the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act, 2008 using Form CTR 160/1, seeking review and setting aside of the CIPC decision; the Tribunal may direct the CIPC to register the name, or the applicant may alternatively submit a fresh name reservation application with a revised name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical street address in South Africa is mandatory under s 23(1)-(3) of the Companies Act, 2008; a serviced or virtual office is permissible for this low-risk online retail activity only if it provides a real, serviceable physical address in South Africa, public accessibility during business hours, and retention of statutory records; a PO Box-only or mail-forwarding-only arrangement is not compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 10% annual probability for a low-risk online retailer of portable solar power products); CIPC may conduct inspections primarily upon complaint or where the FIC raises AML concerns, while SARS retains the right to conduct unannounced visits for VAT and income tax verification purposes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (as amended), ss 13–19, 31 and 66–78; Companies Regulations 2011, regs 7–13; General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 (beneficial ownership disclosure).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic), South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CIPC Form CoR 14.1A) filed together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) through the CIPC e-Services portal; Notice of Registered Office (Form CoR 14.2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a private company (Pty) Ltd under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Each incorporator must subscribe for at least one share, and shares must be issued for adequate consideration. No escrow account is required. The MOI will authorise an initial allotment of 100 no-par value ordinary shares, issued fully paid upon receipt of subscription capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company's incorporation under Companies Act 71 of 2008 is ratified and its Memorandum of Incorporation, as filed with the CIPC, is adopted. FURTHER RESOLVED that the subscribers' allotment of 100 no-par ordinary shares be issued, fully paid, upon receipt of subscription capital. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office and postal address be adopted and CIPC notified. FURTHER RESOLVED that the named first directors are appointed as Chief Executive Officer and Financial Director respectively; that the Accounting Officer is appointed; and that the incorporation agent is authorized to execute statutory filings, engage the auditor, and open the primary banking account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Company Name Reservation and Availability Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the CIPC e-Services portal, complete Form CoR 9.1 with the proposed name and up to two alternate names, and describe the business scope as 'online retail of portable battery generators and solar power equipment'. Pay the name reservation fee electronically using a debit or credit card or EFT. CIPC will screen the proposed name against registered company names, defensive names and trade marks. Name reservations are valid for six months and may be extended once for a further period before incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (completed online)
Certified identity or passport copies of each incorporator
Proof of residential address and FICA/KYC identification documents
Proposed name plus two alternate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of undesirability or similarity, re-file with the alternate names or lodge a formal reconsideration request with CIPC under section 13(5) of the Companies Act. Objections are appealable to the Companies Tribunal, which has jurisdiction over name disputes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal — 'Register a Company' module (Form CoR 14.1A)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1A electronically, attaching the signed Memorandum of Incorporation (standard form CoR 14.1A(c) or a custom-drafted MOI). Capture full names of the incorporators, first directors with signed consents, registered office physical address (not a post office box), accounting officer appointment, and authorised share capital. Pay the statutory incorporation fee (approximately US$10 / ZAR 175). Upon successful examination, CIPC issues the Registration Certificate and the permanent company registration number. The company acquires legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Completed CIPC Form CoR 14.1A
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation
Signed consents of first directors and identity or passport copies
Physical registered office address with proof of address
Proof of electronic payment of the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a deficiency notice or queries a field, correct the defective filing and resubmit through the e-Services portal within the requisition window, normally 21 days. Persistent refusal may be challenged by formal correspondence to the CIPC Registrar; the company must not commence trading until the Registration Certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Governance — First Board Resolution, Share Allotment and Registered Office Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors and company secretary or incorporation agent; CIPC e-Services for statutory registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution of the sole or majority directors adopting the Memorandum of Incorporation, ratifying the subscriber share allotment, adopting the registered office, appointing the Chief Executive Officer and Financial Director, and appointing an Accounting Officer. Open the primary corporate bank account by presenting the incorporation certificate, board resolution, director identity documents and banking mandates. Notify CIPC of any director or registered office changes using the prescribed CoR forms.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution
CIPC Registration Certificate and adopted MOI
Register of members and share issuance records
Directors' registers and declarations
Bank account mandate and director identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any filed form is incomplete, correct and re-file through CIPC e-Services. A defective resolution is cured by passing a subsequent unanimous board resolution ratifying the prior irregularity. Banking mandate queries are resolved by amending the board resolution and resubmitting signed instructions to the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax, VAT and PAYE Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — SARS eFiling portal or SARS branch office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a taxpayer and obtain a corporate income tax reference number. Register for VAT where taxable supplies exceed or are likely to exceed R1 million per annum (mandatory) or R50,000 per annum (voluntary). Register for PAYE, UIF and SDL if employees will be engaged. Authorise the Financial Director as the company's SARS representative and update SARS records with the registered office and director details.
required_dossiers: CIPC Registration Certificate
Memorandum of Incorporation
Identity documents and SARS PIN registrations of directors
Company bank account confirmation
Registered office physical address and supporting utility statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS raises a request for information or a registration query, respond within the prescribed period with the requested documentary evidence. Escalate unresolved issues to the SARS branch office or Taxpayer Service Unit; VAT or income tax registration disputes may proceed through the SARS objection process and, if necessary, the Tax Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing and Company Register Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services — Beneficial Ownership Filing module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Identify all natural persons who directly or indirectly hold 5% or more of the shares or voting rights or exercise effective control of the company. Prepare the Beneficial Ownership register (Form CoR 14.5 / BO1) and submit it through the CIPC e-Services portal within the statutory timeframe after incorporation. Maintain the register of members, directors and prescribed officers, and update CIPC whenever the register changes.
required_dossiers: Completed Beneficial Ownership register (BO1)
Shareholding structure and control-chain documentation
Certified identity copies of beneficial owners holding more than 5%
Board resolution authorising the beneficial ownership submission
CIPC Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BO filing is rejected for data mismatches, reconcile the register against the MOI and shareholder register and resubmit the corrected BO1. Shareholding changes are first filed through the CIPC Amendments module. Penalties apply for non-compliance under the FIC Amendment Act 2022, so timely correction is essential.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Trading Licence and Product Compliance Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality Business/Trading Licensing Office under the Business Act 71 of 1991; National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the e-commerce operation with the local municipal licence office and obtain a business or trading licence if the municipality requires it. Confirm zoning permission for any storage or fulfilment premises. For portable solar and battery products, retain valid Letter of Authority certificates from the NRCS where the company imports or manufactures regulated electrical apparatus, and maintain supplier declarations and Consumer Protection Act 68 of 2008 compliance records for all products sold online.
required_dossiers: CIPC Registration Certificate and MOI
Registered office and storage facility address details
Supplier conformity files and electrical certificate of compliance documents
Municipal business licence application form and zoning clearance
NRCS Letter of Authority copies where the company is importer or manufacturer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal licence queries are cured by submitting the building occupancy certificate and zoning clearance. NRCS Letter of Authority refusals may be re-filed with corrective test reports or appealed through the NRCS adjudication procedure. Product compliance deficiencies must be rectified promptly through corrective action to avoid import or sales embargoes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS), together with the local municipal business and trading licensing authorities under the Business Act 71 of 1991
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business/Trading Licence (Business Act 71 of 1991) and, where the company imports or manufactures regulated electrical apparatus, NRCS Letter of Authority for electrical/electronic products under applicable compulsory specifications

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), South Africa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure online retail of portable solar and battery generators is not a listed activity under EIA Listing Notices 1 to 3 (2017). A Basic Assessment or full Environmental Impact Assessment becomes necessary only if warehousing or storage of hazardous battery or waste streams exceeds prescribed thresholds, in which case a Waste Management Licence under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 may also be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process emissions are associated with online retail operations. Any storage premises must comply with SANS 10142 electrical installation standards and SANS 10400 fire requirements, and must not trigger listed activities under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004. Lithium battery or e-waste handling must comply with the waste segregation and disposal thresholds under NEM:WA, and any discharge must be limited to domestic sewer in accordance with the National Water Act 36 of 1998.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate and Occupancy Certificate issued by the municipal fire authority under the National Building Regulations and SANS 10400 (Parts T and W); Electrical Installation Certificate of Compliance (COC) issued by a registered person under the Electrical Installation Regulations of the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993; structural load clearance for racked storage; and an occupational health and safety workplace clearance for any fulfilment or warehouse space, including a lithium battery storage risk assessment with suitable fire suppression measures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); official taxpayer interface: SARS eFiling at https://efiling.sars.gov.za. Legal-entity incorporation is administered by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) through the BizPortal at https://b-eregistration.cipc.co.za.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned local (Pty) Ltd: incorporate through CIPC (Form CoR14.1 and Memorandum of Incorporation), appoint a South African-resident public officer, activate the eFiling profile, and obtain the company income tax reference number through the SARS-CIPC registration integration. Apply for VAT vendor registration using VAT101 on eFiling as soon as taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period, or elect voluntary VAT registration when taxable supplies have reached at least ZAR 50,000 in the preceding 12 months. For a non-resident company making taxable electronic or digital supplies to South African customers without a local branch, register as a foreign supplier through the SARS eFiling foreign supplier onboarding module, provide certified proof of foreign incorporation and beneficial ownership, appoint a representative vendor or representative taxpayer in South Africa, and obtain a VAT vendor number. Supporting documents must include certified identification documents, a registered or physical business address, a South African bank account for refunds, and a power of attorney if a local agent acts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A proprietary limited company is an opaque resident corporate taxpayer and is not a pass-through entity. It is taxed on worldwide income while resident in South Africa, capital gains are subject to CGT, and distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to Dividends Tax at 20% (subject to applicable treaty relief). No special economic zone or tax-exempt-zone classification applies merely because the company is engaged in e-commerce.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in South Africa. A (Pty) Ltd cannot elect transparent tax treatment. Relevant statutory elections include voluntary VAT registration at the ZAR 50,000 threshold, VAT group registration under section 15 of the VAT Act for connected resident companies, and headquarter company status under section 9I of the Income Tax Act where the qualifying criteria are met. Hybrid mismatch rules contained in the Income Tax Act are mandatory and cannot be elected out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT vendor registration: taxable supplies exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period. Voluntary VAT registration: available if taxable supplies of at least ZAR 50,000 were made in the preceding 12 months. A (Pty) Ltd must register for income tax from incorporation regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate a national real-time fiscal clearance, QR stamp, or digital stamping system for all VAT vendors. Vendors must issue valid tax invoices or reduced tax invoices under section 20 of the VAT Act and retain electronic records for at least five years. Export goods are cleared electronically through the SARS Customs channel using SAD500/DA550 or an approved electronic manifest, and exports may be released only after customs clearance. SARS eFiling provides API-integrated submission of customs declarations, VAT201 returns and status inquiries. SARS is progressively modernising standardised e-invoicing, but digital stamping is not presently required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, movable goods are chargeable at 0% where a vendor supplies the goods to a non-resident customer in the course of a sale, rental or consignment agreement, the goods are physically removed from South Africa, and the goods are exported within the statutory window (normally 90 days from the date of supply, or such extended period as SARS allows). For direct online retail of solar portable power systems and solar panels, zero-rating is claimable where shipping documents show delivery to a foreign destination and contemporaneous customs export evidence is obtained. Services may be zero-rated under section 11(2)(l) only where the services are supplied to a non-resident and are physically used and consumed outside South Africa. The refund mechanism is the VAT201 return; when a zero-rated supply is properly evidenced, no output VAT is declared on the export sale and excess input VAT on export-related costs is refundable by SARS. The burden of proof is on the vendor; inadequate or late export evidence will cause the supply to be reclassified at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial and tax invoice showing the South African seller, overseas buyer/consignee, HS classification description for solar portable power generators or photovoltaic panels, unit prices, and a clear statement of zero-rated export under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act.
SARS customs export declaration (SAD500/DA550 or approved electronic manifest) reflecting the registered exporter, consignee, transport details, and final foreign destination.
Bill of lading, airway bill, or road/rail freight manifest proving physical removal of the goods from South Africa and delivery to an address outside South Africa.

Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorised foreign-exchange dealer in South Africa, supported by bank statements and payment-rail settlement evidence, confirming receipt of the export proceeds in the prescribed manner.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS matches zero-rated export claims against customs cargo declarations, courier and freight transport data, payments received through payment rails such as Stripe and Affirm BNPL, and bank foreign-exchange records. If the required documents are absent, incomplete or materially false, the zero-rating is reversed and VAT at 15% is assessed from the original date of supply, with interest at the prescribed rate. The Tax Administration Act permits conduct-based understatement penalties on the shortfall, together with additional tax under the VAT Act for false export documentation; in cases involving fraud, the additional tax may reach 200% of the VAT shortfall. SARS may also issue a jeopardy assessment, claw back refunds, suspend zero-rated export privileges, and impose criminal liability on directors, the public officer or the representative vendor.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, administered through Authorized Dealers (ADs) which are commercial banks approved under the regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is a floating but non-internationalized currency with residual exchange control. Current-account payments (trade, dividends, interest, royalties) are freely permitted through an AD subject to documentation and the two-leg rule (the ZAR leg must be matched by a foreign-currency leg transiting the same AD). Capital-account convertibility for inward direct investment is open: non-residents may subscribe for 100% of the shares of a South African (Pty) Ltd using foreign currency routed through an AD, with no minimum capital and no prior SARB approval; the AD files a Foreign Investment Declaration (FID; formerly Form F) which becomes the necessary certificate for future remittance of dividends and repatriation of capital. Profit remittance hurdles are tax rather than exchange-control: dividends attract 20% Dividend Withholding Tax (DWT) if not reduced under a Double Taxation Agreement, and the FID-stamped bank record must evidence the non-resident shareholding; interest on shareholder loans is subject to a 15% withholding tax absent treaty relief. Outward capital-account transactions by residents remain restricted (e.g., individuals' R11 million discretionary offshore allowance; corporate outbound investment above prescribed limits requires FinSurv approval).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exports from South Africa require a SARS SAD500 export declaration lodged before goods leave the customs territory. Export proceeds must be received by the exporter within 180 days from the date of shipment (longer maturity is available with AD approval for capital goods); once received in foreign currency, the proceeds must be sold (surrendered) to an AD within 30 days unless credited to an Authorized Dealer-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) where the proceeds may be retained and deployed offshore without conversion. The statutory surrender ratio is effectively 0% if the FCA route is used, and 100% if the exporter has no FCA, because the 30-day rule requires full conversion of the export receipt. E-commerce exports to the Common Monetary Area (Namibia, Lesotho, Eswatini) settle in ZAR freely without FX surrender, as the ZAR is legal tender in the CMA, whereas SADC and other cross-border sales invoiced in USD or EUR are captured by the 180-day/30-day regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - supplementary rail only, not a legal substitute for a South African Authorized Dealer. South Africa does not issue an EU-style EMI licence; cross-border fintech platforms (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Currencycloud) operate under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 by partnering with licensed commercial banks as payment aggregators or payment initiation providers and, where applicable, as FSCA-licensed FSPs. They are practical for disbursing USD to overseas suppliers and for collecting card revenue, but they cannot host SARB-reportable FDI flows, cannot issue an FID, cannot clear ZAR through SAMOS, and must not receive the equity injection because the two-leg rule requires the foreign-currency and ZAR legs to pass through the same AD. Affirm is not a licensed BNPL in South Africa; local BNPL players (Payflex, PayJustNow, Mobicred) clear via the domestic bank rails. Recommended architecture: AD bank as sole FX/FDI treasury backbone; fintech EMIs used only for satellite trade disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical director presence is not mandated for a low-risk e-commerce (Pty) Ltd under FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001). The Big Four banks perform fully remote FICA onboarding for South African-resident directors using electronic identity verification against the Department of Home Affairs database, SABIN and credit-bureau confirmations. For non-resident directors and the 100% foreign parent/UBO, the banks require notarized and Apostilled passport copies, a certified board resolution, a certified copy of the CIPC certificate and Memorandum of Incorporation, proof of registered and trading address, SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin, and a video KYC interview with the relationship manager; the physical branch visit becomes necessary only if the financial crime committee escalates the risk rating due to adverse sanction-screening hits or unresolved source-of-funds matters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity - the shareholder is a non-resident corporate with no filed CIPC Beneficial Ownership register, so the bank cannot identify all natural persons holding 25% or more of ZA_PTY_LTD; the account is blocked under FICA and the General Laws Amendment Act 22 of 2022.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register submission; share register and MOI; corporate organizational chart of the parent; signed UBO declaration; ID/passport copies of ultimate natural owners; registered-agent look-through letter confirming the 25% ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds red flag on the inward equity subscription - the capital injection arrives as a lump-sum cross-border MT103 without a coherent economic narrative, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully signed share subscription agreement; board resolution authorizing the issue; 12 months bank statements and financial statements of the subscribing shareholder; source-of-wealth questionnaire; MT103 reference line reading 'FDI subscription in ZA_PTY_LTD'; prior tax assessment of the shareholder where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax compliance failure - SARS Tax Compliance Status returns 'not compliant' (unfiled returns or outstanding debt), and FICA-linked KYC blocks account opening and Stripe/Payflex settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Active SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin; tax clearance certificate; filed annual company returns at CIPC and tax returns at SARS; IRP6 provisional tax and VAT 201 returns; proof of payment arrangement or SARS TPIN correspondence; SARS importer/exporter customs code registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return for Proprietary Limited Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) of South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days of the anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty tariff increasing with the period of delay; two consecutive years of non-filing may trigger CIPC administrative deregistration (strike-off) without further court process. Continued delinquency also blocks the issuance of compliance status certificates and impairs corporate transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ITR14 Corporate Income Tax Return and Annual Financial Statements submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 12 months of the financial year-end; provisional tax instalments are due at six months of the financial year and at the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment is penalised at 10% per month of the unpaid tax for a maximum of 12 months, and SARS may impose an administrative non-compliance penalty under section 210 of the Tax Administration Act. Understated taxable income exposes the company to understatement penalties ranging from 50% to 150% of the tax shortfall, with criminal prosecution for fraudulent declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: EMP501 Annual Employer Payment Summary (PAYE/UIF/SDL reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May following the 28 February employer tax year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual reconciliation attracts a monthly administrative penalty of ZAR 250 per employee for each month of non-submission (subject to statutory caps). Unpaid PAYE carries a 10% per-month late-payment penalty up to 12 months and can lead to criminal enforcement against directors or employees responsible for withholding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements prepared and presented to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and shareholders under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; not lodged with CIPC for standard private companies unless otherwise required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the company's financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare and present annual financial statements commit a contravention under section 30 of the Companies Act, exposing directors to fines or imprisonment for willful or negligent breach; failure to keep accounting records for 7 years carries separate statutory penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full independent audit is mandatory under section 30 of the Companies Act where the Public Interest Score is 350 or more; where the score is at least 100 and the company has 500 or more shareholders, holds securities in the public interest, or is a regulated entity. Companies scoring 100 to 349 generally require an independent review, while companies below 100 may elect self-review with unanimous shareholder consent unless classified as a regulated company. Public Interest Score components: 1 point per employee, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of turnover, 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party debt, and 1 point per 100 individual shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs for standard private companies, with full IFRS required where the Public Interest Score exceeds 350 or where the company is in a regulated industry; frameworks are set by the Financial Reporting Standards Council under the Companies Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The CIPC Annual Return requires a current beneficial-ownership (BO) declaration as at the filing date. Any share transfer or change of beneficial interest must be filed electronically with CIPC within 7 business days of the change and recorded in the securities register before the next annual return anniversary. The annual return also serves as a confirmation that the register of beneficial interest has been accurately maintained, and directors must certify compliance with section 56 of the Companies Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Directors and Shareholder Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $650–$1,300 per annum (ZAR 1,000–2,000 per month for CIPC registered office address and compliance agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $800–$2,200 for an independent review; $2,500–$8,000 for a full statutory audit dependent on turnover and transaction volume
